newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges firm after low trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges firm after low trade.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges firmed on Thursday after early trade at a low price in a market which some traders said did not reflect fundamentals.
After initial trade at $83 per tonne fob Rotterdam -- or $2 lower than Wednesday's lowest deal -- high sulphur barges moved up to change hands at $85 then $86 a tonne.
Late offers were in the $86 range, or $1 up on some of Wedensday's late offers.
"They are just playing games in Rotterdam," one trader said. "I just think someone tried to push the market down but it did not work and now they are trying to set higher numbers."
Others agreed. Traders said bunker demand continued poor, with one saying: "There is no real physical market, not that much bunker demand."
Some traders said Rotterdman material was in short supply.

No high sulphur cargoes were heard traded early in the Rotterdman area but traders said a cargo of Russian E-4 was heard bought on Wednesday by a British major at three means plus $2.50 -- a price said to be reflective of current market value.
"Most (Russian) cargoes are finding buyers and supplies are stable. It seems to be easy to find a buyer with the low E-4 premium," one regular buyer of Russian material said.
